m: Yalova Province (Turkish: Yalova ili) is a province in northwestern Turkey, on the eastern coast of the Sea of Marmara. Its adjacent provinces are Bursa to the south and Kocaeli to the east. Its area is 798 km2 (making it the smallest province of Turkey), and its population is 296,333 (2022). Prior to 1930, the area around Yalova constituted a district of Kocaeli Province; from 1930 to 1995, it was part of Istanbul Province; in 1995, the area was separated and made into the current Yalova Province. The provincial capital is the city of Yalova.

Q2601948: Termal is a town in Yalova Province in the Marmara region of Turkey. It is the seat of Termal District. Its population is 3,409 (2022). It is renowned for its hot springs, Yalova Thermal Baths (Turkish: Termal). It is about 80 km away from Istanbul. The huge hot springs complex, lying on a land of about 1.6 square kilometres, is located 12 km away from Yalova. There are four hotels in the complex, one of which is an aparthotel. There are also five baths which possess historical value. The mayor is Hüseyin Sinan Acar (AK Party).
Q8047515: Yalova Atatürk Mansion (Turkish: Yalova Atatürk Köşkü) is a mansion built for and used by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk during his visits to the thermal facilities in Yalova at Marmara region, Turkey. Currently, the building is owned by the Turkish Grand National Assembly and is partly open to public as a house museum.
Q21288238: The Walking Pavilion (Yürüyen Köşk) is a rectangular, two-storey, part-masonry pavilion built in 1929 on the Yalova National Farm.
Q97320238: Sudüşen Waterfall is on the Nacaklı stream, 8 km from the Üvezpınar quarter in Yalova, at an altitude of about 250 metres. Tours run from Yalova (43 km); a 120-metre panorama hill overlooks the falls, and the pool below is suitable for swimming.
Q4794056: The Armutlu Peninsula (Turkish: Armutlu Yarımadası) is a peninsula extending westward into Marmara Sea in the Anatolian section of Turkey. In addition to Yalova Province, parts of Kocaeli Province and Bursa Province are on the peninsula.
Q20988558: The Yalova Earthquake Monument (Turkish: Yalova Deprem Anıtı), a.k.a. 17 August 1999 Earthquake Monument (Turkish: 17 Ağustos 1999 Deprem Anıtı), is a monument to commemorate the victims of the 1999 İzmit earthquake in Yalova, Turkey. Situated in the 17 August Memorial Park in Yalova, it was opened at the first anniversary of the earthquake on August 17, 2000.
Q38251251:
Harmankaya Nature Park (Turkish: Harmankaya Tabiat Parkı) is a nature park located in Termal district of Yalova Province, northwestern Turkey.
Harmanlı Nature Park is located 18 km (11 mi) to Yalova, 6 km (3.7 mi) to Termal and 5 km (3.1 mi) to Üvezpınar village, and situated south of Termal district on the road between Üvezpınar and Sudüşen Waterfall close to the provincial border to Bursa. The area covering 1 ha (2.5 acres), which formerly had a registered recreational area status, was declared a nature park by the Ministry of Environment and Forest on July 11, 2011.
Q85969061: Bozburun Lighthouse is a lighthouse in the Armutlu district of Yalova.
Q134592335: Erikli Waterfall is a natural waterfall near the village of Teşvikiye in the Termal district of Yalova. Its natural beauty and cool air draw visitors especially in summer.
Q132682131: The museum building is the house where Atatürk stayed in Yalova before the Walking Pavilion was built. It was restored in 1981 and opened as a museum displaying his belongings.
